svg.title: A-000 Site Plan — Detached Villa
svg.text: S T R E E T
9.50 × 13.50 m — four storeys and a penthouse
Masonry wall cut by section — 200 mm
Internal stud or block partition, 120 mm
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. Final draft — layout agreed. The villa is detached: set
back 1.00 m from the west, north and east boundaries, the
three sides a neighbour stands on. The south is not set
back — it faces the street across our own forecourt.
2. Footprint 9.50 × 13.50 m = 128.2 m² on a 264.5 m² plot,
48.5 % coverage against 63.0 % for the attached scheme at
P4. Detaching costs 22 % of each floor and buys an open
aspect on all four sides and no party wall.
3. The setbacks are our own land, so each is a 1.00 m paved
side passage rather than a dead strip, reached from the
forecourt on the east and from the entrance garden on the
4. The cantilever oversails the forecourt by 2.00 m at the
west end and 1.50 m at the east, leaving at least 1.50 m
clear to the street, and covers the front door and its
three risers. Nothing projects over a boundary, but the
overhang is subject to the local projection rule; confirm
5. The client's survey sketch recorded a 0.50 m step in the
north boundary and a 5.50 m offset between the two blocks'
north walls; the two cannot both be true. Resolved in
favour of a straight boundary at 18.00. To be confirmed by
measured survey before any work starts on site.
6. Structure is an RC frame on the grid shown, 300 mm columns
on wall centrelines so none stands in a room. The A-300
enlargements are the last sheets still on the old 11.50 ×
Final draft — layout agreed with the client; not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
P11 2026-10-07 penthouse: 2.51 m corridor outside the flat; living room to the face
P12 2026-10-07 bedrooms numbered 1-11; all five floors issued as final draft
P13 2026-10-07 site plan redrawn for the detached villa
P14 2026-10-07 section A-A recut through the east strip, and marked on every plan
